issue.title: sase tool run never prints the run id when the child fails to launch (127/126), so the recorded run is unreachable
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-135.7 (epic sase-135, "Named tools and the foreground ToolRun ledger") as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note; filed by the sase-135 land agent on 2026-09-20.

A `sase tool run` invocation whose child never starts — the executable is missing (exit 127) or is not executable (exit 126) — still records a settled ToolRun in the ledger, but the wrapper never prints the `sase tool run <run-id>` header line it prints for a run that does start. The user therefore has a durable record they cannot address: there is no id on screen to pass to `sase tool show`, and recovering it means listing `sase tool runs` and guessing which row was the failed launch.

This is the inverse of the fail-open contract the epic's DoD-5 establishes. Fail-open is about never claiming a durable identity that does not exist; this gap is about not disclosing a durable identity that does exist.

Remediation: print the wrapper header before attempting the spawn (or on the spawn-failure path), so every recorded run id reaches the user exactly once. Keep the exact-once execution and exit-code guarantees intact — DoD-2 requires the child's own stdout/stderr and exit status to survive unchanged, and the header must stay on stderr so a wrapped command's stdout is still byte-exact.

task_type_fields.impact: Anyone who hits a typo'd or missing executable under sase tool run. The run is recorded but its id is never shown, so sase tool show cannot be used on it without manually scanning sase tool runs. Low blast radius, but it breaks the ledger's core promise that every recorded run is addressable.
task_type_fields.repro: cd into a SASE checkout with a built .venv, then run: .venv/bin/sase tool run -- /nonexistent/binary ; observe exit 127 and no 'sase tool run <id>' line on stderr, then run .venv/bin/sase tool runs and see the settled row that was never announced. Repeat with a non-executable file for the 126 case.

payload.description: Both sit on the sase tool run spawn-failure path (127/126): sase-141 makes the recorded run id reachable there, sase-145 makes the typed failure reason durable. Fixing them together avoids two passes over the same executor branch.
